speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng
text: asked the Minister for Education (Schools) (a) how many appeals for exemption from Mother Tongue Language (MTL) have been received in each of the last three years; (b) what are the reasons for the appeals and what are the outcomes of these appeals; and (c) which department in the Ministry is responsible for assessing the appeals for an exemption from MTL and what is their basis for the approval of the appeals.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Ministers for Education (Ms Low Yen Ling) (for the Minister for Education)
text: Under our bilingual policy, students are required to offer English and a Mother Tongue Language (MTL).

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Ministers for Education (Ms Low Yen Ling) (for the Minister for Education)
text: The panel comprises specialists with expertise in curriculum provisions and SEN.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Ministers for Education (Ms Low Yen Ling) (for the Minister for Education)
text: Depending on the complexity of the case, the panel may also consult clinicians in the healthcare sector in their evaluations of the applications.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Ministers for Education (Ms Low Yen Ling) (for the Minister for Education)
text: Students with difficulties in reading and writing MTL can take up Foundation MTL in Primary 5 and Primary 6, and the MTL "B" curriculum at secondary and junior college levels.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Ministers for Education (Ms Low Yen Ling) (for the Minister for Education)
text: The Foundation MTL and MTL "B" curriculum focuses on the development of oral and listening skills, with a reduced demand on writing skills.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Ministers for Education (Ms Low Yen Ling) (for the Minister for Education)
text: This allows them to continue to have exposure to learning MTL.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: I strongly support MOE's direction for bilingualism and for several reasons linked to our heritage, our roots and our culture.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: I have received quite a number of appeals and a lot of concerns as well from some families.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: So, I am wondering if MOE has used this tool of exemption very bluntly, so bluntly that the families are really struggling and even thinking of future plans whether they should remain in the local education system after the compulsory education years.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: So, one, I would like to ask MOE if we can relook at the ways by which we make these decisions.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: Can we finetune these decisions and consider those cases with merit, especially if they are strongly supported by a very well-respected psychologist and psychiatrist in the field?

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: Also, finally, to ask if MOE can more creatively come up with more ideas so that people who go through this system of learning MTL do not end up hating it or disliking it so much and dropping it the minute they officially can.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: So, I want to assure her on that.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: I also want to reiterate that MTL exemption is granted to students with SEN.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: Allow me to just share some of the considerations by the MOE panel.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: First and foremost, when we receive an application, we will look at the diagnosis by the psychologist that they had submitted.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: Two, we will also liaise with the student's school to understand how the student is managing his or her learning.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: Three, we will work with the school to better understand if the student is responding well to the teaching and instruction during the MTL lessons.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: All these are important inputs for the decision.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: The fourth consideration that we look at is how well the student is coping with the overall studies.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: For students who submit MTL-exemption applications on grounds of SEN, these are the four key considerations.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: I mentioned earlier that we do review the criteria from time to time.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: I also want to assure Members that MOE Headquarters takes every MTL-exemption application seriously.

speaker: Mr Yee Chia Hsing (Chua Chu Kang)
text: I have received feedback that some of the families have been working abroad for many years and their kids grew up overseas.

speaker: Mr Yee Chia Hsing (Chua Chu Kang)
text: In their case, when they come back, the children are supposed to enter secondary school and they have to suddenly study MTL when they do not even speak a single word of Mandarin.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: The first group will be students who are severely affected because of their SEN.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: The second group will be students who join our Singapore education system mid-stream, and they did not have the opportunity to learn MTL.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: So, yes, we do consider the application for MTL exemption by the group that is highlighted by Mr Yee.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: I want to assure Mr Yee that for those applications, we would evaluate factors like the applicants' learning history, previous country of residence, admission level and also, the extent of home language environment.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng
text: As a follow-up to Mr Yee's question, I would like to ask the Senior Parliamentary Secretary if it is true that one of the factors of consideration is that the child or the applicant must fail every subject before they can be exempted from MTL?

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng
text: I would like MOE to consider, in the spirit of lifelong learning, if there is any way by which it could convene a group so that we can continue with this learning of MTL or other languages that are useful or of interest, for the longer term, beyond the formal school years.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: I did share the four key factors that the MOE panel will consider.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: And one consideration is how well they are coping in their overall study, whether there is a need for us to make adjustment to the student's total academic load.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: It is worthwhile for me to take a few seconds to reiterate that in MOE, we are committed to support and enable every student to learn MTL at a level that he or she is capable of, something that Ms Denise Phua earlier said that she was fully supportive of.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: This is why the MTL curriculum is differentiated to cater to the needs of students based on their varying abilities.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: We do have students with SEN who have chosen to take Foundation MTL at Primary 5 and Primary 6.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: The focus of the Foundation MTL is to help them to develop a strong foundation in their oral and listening skills, with less demand on writing.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: So, there are students who have chosen to take Foundation MTL so that they can build up their foundation in MTL as the parents know bilingualism is advantageous to the child.
